passage:
Divyansh texts his friend Mohit during a lunch break.

Divyansh: He made me redo the whole sheet at 9pm again. Called me useless in front of the client.
Mohit: bro just quit
Divyansh: Can't. Papa's medicines and my sister's fees run on my salary. It's not weakness, it's just the maths right now.
Mohit: True. Sorry. So what do you do?
Divyansh: Stay, but not swallow it whole. I keep a note on my phone with dates. I eat lunch away from my desk and switch off at eight even if he pings. Two applications every Sunday.
Mohit: That's an actual plan.
Divyansh: I keep hearing "everyone gets shouted at, it's normal". It's not normal, Mohit. It's just where I am for now.
Mohit: Agreed. This Sunday I'll help with your CV.

qa.q: How many applications does Divyansh send every Sunday?
qa.a: Divyansh sends two applications every Sunday.

qa.q: How does Divyansh feel about staying in the job?
qa.a: Divyansh feels stuck but clear-eyed: quitting is not possible because Papa's medicines and the sister's fees run on the salary, and Divyansh refuses to think of the shouting as normal.

qa.q: How is Divyansh protecting his dignity and health while staying?
qa.a: He keeps dated notes, eats lunch away from his desk, switches off at eight and sends two applications every Sunday, so he is planning a way out.

qa.q: How does Mohit's view change during the chat?
qa.a: Mohit first says to just quit, then accepts the money constraint, calls it an actual plan and offers to help with the CV. 🤍

grounding: Divyansh needs the salary for his family and swallows the abuse, staying while planning a way out and refusing to call it normal.
